name: Ui_LayoutElement_UpdateTransformFlags
signature: void Ui_LayoutElement_UpdateTransformFlags(LayoutElement* self, LayoutAnimState* state, * u32 flags)

name: Actor_AimAtPoint
summary: Rotates an actor model to face a world-space point: builds the model basis, clamps the angle to about +/-90 degrees, applies the yaw through the quaternion helpers and finally calls Math_Vec3_LookAtRotationMatrix on self->f_28.
evidence: The old "Camera_" label was wrong: the new callers are Actor_Action_SkullRun_Update and maybe_Actor_Action_SkullRun_Start, both passing their action object plus the vector returned by maybe_Actor_SkullRun_ComputeScreenVector, and every matrix write goes to self->f_28 (the actor model). No camera object appears anywhere in the body.

summary: Character-specific pose update built on the model's "Skull_Run" node: forces that animation node, derives the facing basis and the acos angle from the node position, stores the relative offset and hands the aim to Math_Vec3_LookAtRotationMatrix.

evidence: Still no caller; support is only the vtable slot 0x77DA48 next to the sibling action methods, the "Skull_Run" literal and the maybe_Node_ComputeAttachedTransform callee. The "Battle" part is a guess from the vtable neighbourhood.

name: Text_LayoutMeasureCharacterWidths
summary: Measuring pass over a laid-out text row: for each of the f_466 character codes at layout+0x416 it resolves the character record and accumulates its signed advance/offset into the per-class width accumulators (f_BEC..f_C68, punctuation, digits, full-width), then finalises through func_0045B22C.
evidence: The caller is now Text_Layout_RunPass, so this is the measure pass of the text layout. The two Item_LookupRecord calls at the top only fetch two item category bytes into scratch locals (ids read from layout+6/+8); the loop itself is glyph data (class byte +8, advance +10), so this is not item code.

name: Text_Row_CheckChanceGate
signature: u64 Text_Row_CheckChanceGate(float * self, u32 arg2, int arg3)
summary: Chance gate for one text row: derives a percentage from the row definition (base value minus 10 per character and a 50-point penalty when the row type was not accepted), rolls the battle RNG in [1,100] and returns 1 only when the roll is inside the threshold.
evidence: The old "CalcRowPenalty" was wrong: the only caller Text_Row_TryLayout does "if (maybe_Text_CalcRowPenalty(def, args+8, accepted) == 0) return -1;", i.e. a show/don't-show gate. The callee at work+0x4218 is the battle RNG (func_001CA474 = roll in [lo,hi], FACTS.md), so the function rolls a percentage, it does not compute a text baseline.

name: Text_MeasureRowByType
signature: int Text_MeasureRowByType(int arg1, int arg2, int arg3)
summary: Measures one row by fixed kind (0x8C/0x8D/0x8E map to types 2/0x40/0x3E): fills a 0x4A0-byte layout context, lays the text out and stores the resulting width/height at row+4.
evidence: The callers are now Battle_Ui_PartyPanel_BuildRowTextC/D, i.e. the battle party-panel row builders, and the id-to-type mapping 0x8C/0x8D/0x8E -> 2/0x40/0x3E is unchanged.

name: maybe_Monster_IsImmuneToStatus

name: Battle_Monster_GetHpBarRatio

summary: Computes the MP-bar fill of a battle monster: takes the record max at f_24, compares the current ratio with 1% and marks the layout dirty on a change; the value is returned in s0.
evidence: Same evidence as 0x4900A8: Battle_Monster_GetHpBarValue reads the result from in_s0 and picks the larger of the two, so this is the MP fill getter (Ghidra dropped the VFP return).

name: Ui_ItemListCore_SetMode
